proofUses.reason: Counting the first forbidden reversal distinguishes n=2 from later steps and proves the absolute convergence domain.
The scalar recurrence and the directional matrix inverse give the same quotient. The random-walk series comparison is asserted on the real subcritical interval.
The bipartite-frequency length series fails the term test. Its radial value is retained, and the spatial Fourier density is justified only in the integrable dimensions.
A deterministic set-difference identity uses the actual deleted set and surviving endpoints. The target-outside-cluster condition is supplied by pivotality, not by definition.
Exact elimination retains Fourier-shift signs, the connector parameter and the negative correction. Matrix invertibility and scalar nonvanishing are separate conditions.
